summary: Final SSE event merged with health probe on edge layer causing unclosed JSON and truncated image embed
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteServe reports intermittent truncation of the final SSE event when reconnecting after a short edge-level probe. The final JSON choice is left unclosed and an inline image URL (base64/attachment) is missing. The customer observed this with our JS SDK behind their corporate gateway.

Impact:
- Affected users see final paragraph missing or truncated image/attachment in ~0.7% of reconnects for long outputs (>4k tokens).
- Causes downstream parsing errors in customer app (JSON.parse errors or missing attachments).
- Reported by a production customer on Dedicated plan; affects live user workflows.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted endpoint in us-west-2, dedicated cluster (cust-dc-7).
- Customer uses our JS SDK v1.4.2 behind an internal HTTP/2 reverse proxy (company gateway v2.9) that performs active health probes.
- Models: redwood-3b, streaming SSE mode with keepalive heartbeats every 20s.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Start a long streaming generation that includes an inline image URL at the end (embedding produced as base64).
2. Simulate a short edge-level health probe during the final 1-2 seconds of generation (their gateway does this automatically).
3. Client reconnects (SSE re-establish) and receives output; final JSON block is unclosed or missing image field.

Observed behavior:
- The last SSE event appears concatenated with a small health-probe frame from the gateway. The client-side parser sees a malformed final JSON chunk (trailing comma/no closing bracket) or missing "attachments" field. The generation content itself appears complete on the server but gets truncated on the client.

Expected behavior:
- Final SSE event should be delivered intact across reconnects. Heartbeat/probe frames should not be merged into payload frames in a way that corrupts JSON boundaries.

Logs & attachments:
- Customer provided client-side console log: "Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input" with SSE payload snippet.
- Server trace from prod (partial): "stream:choice:finalized id=... status=ok size=... flush_ts=2026-03-12T17:45:03Z"
- Edge capture (pcap excerpt) attached by SRE shows two minimal frames coalesced at the proxy.

Reproduction note:
- We can reproduce locally by inserting a small TCP-level delay and running an HTTP/2 multiplexing proxy configured to aggressively batch small frames; leads to the same corrupted final event.

investigation_notes: Edge pcap analysis: gateway coalesces consecutive small DATA frames into a single packet when probe arrives within 15ms of final payload. Coalesced payload shows final SSE event JSON immediately followed by probe marker bytes (non-printable) — client SDK treats whole block as one event and fails JSON parse.
Local repro: using 'h2proxy' configured to "batch-small-frames=true" reproduces issue deterministically for large outputs where final flush is <64 bytes.
Server-side traces: finalization path does call flush but previously relied on nagle-like buffering; small finalizer packets could be merged by upstream TCP/H2 muxers.

Hypothesis validated: two mitigations reduce failure rate to zero in tests: (1) ensure final SSE event ends with unambiguous delimiter sequence and force immediate socket flush; (2) instruct proxies to avoid coalescing for SSE endpoints.
Decision: implement (1) in runtime; recommend (2) as ops mitigation for customers with aggressive gateways.
Related: INT-4453 contains internal notes from a similar case in staging where HTTP/2 server push altered chunk boundaries; reuse learnings on forced-flush semantics.

Risk assessment: patch is low-risk (finalization path only). Must ensure sentinel doesn't break existing parsers; used sequence is double-newline + zero-byte marker which SDKs will ignore in normal flow (SDKs updated to strip sentinel).
resolution: Fix applied: runtime PR merged (pr/4021) to append a safe sentinel ("\n\n\u0000") to final SSE events and call immediate flush on the final buffer. SDK change: js-sdk v1.4.3 will strip sentinel on client side.
Workaround: customers can set js-sdk option preferFlushOnComplete=true to force client-side flush behavior until runtime patch is deployed.
Deployment: canary rolled 2026-03-14 12:00 UTC; prod rollout completed 2026-03-14 20:00 UTC. Monitoring for 72h; no recurrence in customer tests to date.

Follow-up actions: (a) Update knowledge base article on streaming reconnect behavior and recommended proxy settings; (b) Add a server-side trace tag for final-event-flush to alert if coalescing observed in future; (c) Reach out to top-10 dedicated customers with guidance on proxy configs.
Status: Resolved for customer with patch deployed and customer-confirmed mitigation. Ticket remains open until end of 72h monitoring window.
